summary: The phones run an agent's ```html-live page from the message text they already have, instead of only showing the desktop's still image. This PR adds the shared rules (src/shared/html-live-phone.ts): the phone document puts our bytes first (the CSP meta, the guard script, the libraries on iOS, the theme, the import map and the size reporter) so no page byte runs before the CSP; the phone CSP allows only the page's own origin (Android), data: and blob:, with default-src, form-action and base-uri 'none'; the guard removes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection, RTCDataChannel, Notification and service worker registration, reports CSP violations, and caps page console output at 50 lines a second, with a separate budget for its own height and blocked lines; htmlLivePhoneVerdict refuses an open fence, the desktop cap and library list, and mermaid (desktop only); phoneLiveRunning gives one slot to the full-screen view or the most visible page once the list is still for 300 ms, needs Run on a phone under 3 GB RAM and after a crash, and blocks a key after two crashes; the iOS message parser reads only {t:'h'|'e'|'b'} under 1 KB, and a per-second gate caps reads at 100. Accepted rest risk (user decision 2026-10-29): CSP does not cover WebRTC, and a page can take a clean RTCPeerConnection from an about:blank iframe, so it can reveal the phone's IP over STUN. The page holds nothing the agent could not already send from the desktop. Revisit if a page ever holds data the agent could not send itself. Every phone surface is staged behind phone_html_live_run, off by default. The iOS app (Settings > Chat > Run live pages, a local setting, off) runs one page at a time in a WebView that loads one HTML string with no base URL, refuses every load after the first about:blank, keeps no data, and reads only the capped message channel; inline it takes no touches and a tap opens a full-screen view. The app cannot read the phone's memory (no device-info module, and adding one needs a native build), so every iPhone counts as low on RAM and waits for Run. originWhitelist is ['*'], not ['about:blank']: react-native-webview hands a URL outside the list to Linking.openURL before onShouldStartLoadWithRequest runs, so a narrower list would let a page open https:, tel: or sms: links in other apps; the navigation gate is the filter. Libraries: chart.js, d3, three and OrbitControls ship in both apps (about 1.2 MB raw). Android takes resources/sb-live as an assets folder, so each is an asset at its /_sb/ path next to its licence. The Expo app gets .sblib copies in apps/mobile/assets/live-libs (metro takes no .js asset), written by scripts/build-visual-host.mjs; the iOS view reads only the ones a page names, for that run only. Mermaid does not ship on phones.

desktop.reason: The desktop already runs html-live pages in its own sandbox (src/main/ide/html-preview-*). The phone rules add an optional import map argument to htmlLiveHead; the desktop passes none and its document is byte for byte unchanged (tests/unit/html-live.test.ts).

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing is stored on the backend. The page comes from the message text already on the phone, the libraries ship in the app, and the crash counts live in memory for one app run. The iOS switch is one new key in the app's persisted preferences; a store without it reads the default (off), so no migration. No table, settings row or wire field changes; older desktops and phones are unaffected.

automated: tests/unit/html-live-phone.test.ts: the CSP meta comes before every page byte for a fragment, a full document, a script before <head> and a <head> inside a comment, with and without inlined libraries; a leading doctype is removed; iOS inlines only the named libraries (classic as scripts, three and OrbitControls in the import map, mermaid never); every fetch directive refuses https, LAN, loopback, ws, wss, file:, content:, intent: and another page's origin on both origins; the verdict, run slot, low-RAM rule, crash rule, message and console parsers and the rate gate; the fixture equals the builder.

tests/unit/html-live-phone-sandbox.test.ts (headless Chromium, run here with SB_CHROMIUM set to Playwright's chrome-headless-shell 1248): a probe page tries fetch (internet, 10.0.2.2, 127.0.0.1), XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, a worker, (internet, LAN, file:), CSS url(), @import, @font-face, a stylesheet link, preload and prefetch, an iframe, an object, a video, a script and a form post. With the Android header CSP on https://tok.sb-live.invalid and with the meta CSP alone on an opaque page, no request reaches the network layer and no WebSocket opens; fetch, XHR and both RTCPeerConnection names throw; the guard reports blocked URLs. A copy of the CSP with connect-src and img-src set to * fails the test (ten requests leak). A three page imports data: modules through the import map. A page that writes 60 error lines in its first second still reports its height (the height and blocked lines have their own budget), the bridge gets only {t,v} reports, at most 50 page lines a second, a log of a null-prototype object does not throw, and the engine reports no error for the CSP itself.

tests/unit/visual-host-asset.test.ts: the .sblib copies are exactly the libraries the phones ship (all but mermaid) and equal resources/sb-live byte for byte. Android LiveLibraryAssetsTest (Robolectric): each library and licence opens as an asset at its /_sb/ path with the vendored bytes.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

iOS jest (apps/mobile/src/components/__tests__/HtmlLiveFrame.test.tsx, HtmlLiveCard.test.tsx, screens/__tests__/app-shell-parity.test.tsx): every WebView prop of the live view (source {html} with no baseUrl, javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically false, no onOpenWindow, incognito, cacheEnabled false, allowsLinkPreview false, dataDetectorTypes none, allowsInlineMediaPlayback false, mediaCapturePermissionGrantType deny, allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures false, textInteractionEnabled and scrollEnabled false inline and true full screen, the guard as injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded); onShouldStartLoadWithRequest allows only the first about:blank load and refuses https, http, file:, content:, intent:, market:, tel:, sms:, mailto:, javascript:, data:, blob: a second about:blank and a window.open or target=_blank load; the library's own whitelist path with our originWhitelist ['*'] never calls Linking while ['about:blank'] would hand a refused URL to Linking.openURL; the document starts with the CSP meta and carries default-src, connect-src, img-src, style-src, font-src and form-action, with no remote host or wildcard; only the named libraries are read, as data: URLs; three needs iOS 16.4; the message channel drops non-schema, oversize and over-rate messages, caps errors and blocked URLs at 20, debounces height to 100 ms and never calls Linking or Clipboard; the 8 s watchdog, a second onLoadStart and a WebContent crash stop the page; the card shows no Run with the flag off, a failed verdict or a mermaid page (with the desktop-only note), needs Run (memory unknown), runs one page with no touches inline, opens a full-screen view, keeps the row height on a swap, stops on leaving view, blur and background, shows This page stopped and Run again after a crash and no Run after two, and keeps Source, Copy source and Open on desktop; the Settings switch is off by default.
notExercised: No phone runs a page yet: the Android and iOS WebViews come in plan PRs 4 and 5.
The Chromium sandbox test is skipped where no Chromium is installed (CI has none); it ran on this Mac.
Android System WebView and WKWebView may differ from desktop Chromium; the instrumented device probe (plan PR 4) and an iPhone probe run are the proof for each phone.
The WebRTC rest risk through an about:blank iframe is accepted, not tested.
Nothing proves the WKWebView sandbox until the probe page runs on a real iPhone; the flag stays off in store builds until then.

The phones have no third-party notices screen. The Android APK carries licence files for chart.js, d3 and three (three's covers OrbitControls). The iOS bundle carries the vendored source headers where present: chart.js and three have licence headers, d3 has a copyright header, and OrbitControls has none. A notices screen is not built.
